items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to the requirement for fingerprinting of licensed professionals under Title VIII of such law, access to patient or client records in the investigation and prosecution of professional licensing and misconduct proceedings and summary suspension of professional licenses
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S7791

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the education law, in relation to
the requirement for fingerprinting of licensed professionals under
Title VIII of such law, access to patient or client records in the
investigation and prosecution of professional licensing and misconduct
proceedings and summary suspension of professional licenses

 PURPOSE :

To provide for criminal background checks for licensed professionals.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1. Amends education law section 6501 to provide for a criminal
history records search upon admission to a profession under the
jurisdiction of the New York State Education Department (SED). This
provision further provides that all professions under SED's purview,
in order to be admitted, all applicants must be of good moral
character as determined by SED in regulations.

Subdivision 3 of new section 6501 further provides that starting on
July 1, 2017 when SED receive an application for professional
licensure, SED must initiate a criminal history records search in
accordance with New York State Division of Criminal Justice Services
(DCJS) rules and regulations. SED shall also provide the applicant
with a form proscribed under law prior to initiating the
fingerprinting process in order to obtain the applicant's consent to
the background check as a condition of licensure

The form shall inform the applicant that SED is required to request
criminal history information from DCJS and the FBI and review this
information and that the applicant has the right to review and seek
correction of this information pursuant to regulations and procedures
established by DOS.

SED must obtain signed, informed consent of the applicant which
indicates that the applicant has been informed of the right and
procedures necessary to obtain, review and seek correction of criminal
history information, the reason for the request, consent of such
request, supplied a current mailing address for the applicant,
informed and the applicant may withdraw an application for licensure
without prejudice at any time before the licensed is issued regardless
of whether SED reviewed the applicant's criminal history information,
informed that in the event of a denied license that SED must notify
DCJS of the denial of licensure and DCJS must destroy that applicant's
fingerprints and the applicant had been informed of the manner in
which he or she may submit any information in regard to good conduct
and rehabilitation.

The subdivision further provides the appropriate fees. It further
provides that if SED determines that the applicant may not have the
proper moral character for licensure based upon the applicant's
criminal history record, the applicant must be afforded notice and a
hearing to offer proof in opposition to such determination in
accordance with SED regulations. SED must require applicants for
licensure to submit fingerprints and DCJS and the FBI shall forward
the criminal history record to SED in a timely manner. This also
provides that there shall be no cause of action against the SED
Commissioner, DCJS or their officers or employees for damages related
to the dissemination of criminal history background records when said
parties have reasonable and in good faith relied upon the accuracy of
this information.

Subdivision 4 of the section provides that all licensed professionals
shall be required to report to SED within 30 days any record of a
conviction of a crime and/or any pending criminal charges. Licensees
must also report to SED within 30 days any charges of professional
misconduct in any jurisdiction and/or any adverse actions undertaken
by a hospital, institution or employer as result of the licensee's
professional duties.

Failure of a licensee to provide such information shall be grounds for
professional misconduct under the education law. SED must promulgate a
form to be provided to all licensees on which they must report any
charges defined herein. All records processed pursuant to subdivision
4 must be confidential and must not be published or in any way
disclosed to persons other than SED personnel.. Upon receipt of a
report from a licensee that they have been subject to a criminal
conviction or disciplinary action, SED may refer the report to the
professional conduct officer for an investigation of potential
disciplinary action. If a licensed professional is convicted of an
crime, the District Attorney (DA) must provide notice to SED and SED
must proceed to determine whether the individual possess good moral
character without delay.

Section 2. Amends education law section 6510 to provide for SED to
have the ability to perform a summary action as part of discipline for
misconduct in relation to licensure. Whenever the SED commissioner or
h is her designee is presented with information indicating that a
licensee or a registered entity is causing or engaging in conduct
which has resulted in patient and/or client harm and if in the
commissioner's opinion it would be prejudicial to the interests of the
people to delay action until an opportunity for a hearing can be
provided or after an investigation and a recommendation by the SED
commissioner that a licensee is causing or engaging in conduct which
constitutes an imminent danger to the heath and/or safety of the
people, the commissioner may order the licensee by written notice to
discontinue such dangerous conduct and suspend any privileges to
practice the profession or take certain action immediately for a
period of 90 days from the date of service of the order. Within 10
days from service of the order, SED shall schedule a hearing and the
hearing must be completed within 90 days of the service of the order.
The SED commissioner shall first determine whether by a preponderance
of the evidence the licensee is eng aging in an activity which
constitutes imminent danger or harm to the health of the people.

Section 3. Amends education law 6560(8) to provide that a professional
conduct officer may examine and obtain records of patients or clients
in any investigation or proceeding by SED acting within the scope of
its authorization. Any information obtained shall be confidential and
shall not be further disclosed except to the extent necessary for the
proper function of SED without express consent.

Section 4. Sets for the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

In April 2016, ProPublica released an investigation into discipline
practices for nurses across the State of New (http://ww.
propublica.org/ article/weak-oversigh -lets-dangerous-nurses -work-
innew-york). This legislation is intended to be a start in remedying
issues laid out with the discipline process through the New York State
Education (SED) for licensure of professions under the jurisdiction.

Previously, New York did not have the ability for summary suspensions
for cases of imminent harm and providing SED with this tool will help
streamline the disciplinary process in severe cases. Further, criminal
background checks were only performed for prospective teachers and no
other licensed professionals under SED's jurisdiction.


Ultimately, the Legislature is committed to make sure that the public
is protected and the best way to achieve this goal is to take an
intense look at the current process. It is important that all
applicants for a license for a profession under SED's jurisdiction are
fingerprinted and a background check is provided before that person
receives clearance for a license. Especially for the health care
professions, it is important that those providing services to the
citizens of New York State are of the highest moral character
standards and that there are protections in place for New Yorkers if
any licensed professionals run afoul of this standard.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New bill

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
On the 180th day after it shall have become law.

A.actClause: AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to the requirement for fingerprinting of licensed professionals under Title VIII of such law, access to patient or client records in the investigation and prosecution of professional licensing and misconduct proceedings and summary suspension of professional licenses
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S7791A

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the education law, in relation to access to patient or
client records in the investigation and prosecution of professional
licensing and misconduct proceedings and summary suspension of
professional licenses

 PURPOSE :

This bill would enhance and strengthen the State Education
Department's (SED) disciplinary process for licensed professionals.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1. Requires all licensed professionals to meet moral character
requirements as defined by SED; requires all licensed professionals to
report to SED all criminal convictions and/or pending charges and any
charges of professional misconduct in any jurisdiction and/or any
adverse actions undertaken by a hospital or employer within 30 days;
provides that all records submitted to SED shall remain confidential;
provides that when a licensed professional reports a criminal
conviction, a SED professional conduct officer can initiate an
investigation of potential disciplinary action and; requires District
Attorneys to provide notice to SED when a licensed professional is
convicted of a crime.

Section 2. Establishes a summary suspension preceding that allows SED
to temporarily suspend a professional license if such individual is
causing or engaging in conduct that poses an imminent danger to the
health and/or safety of the people while an investigation and hearing
process takes place.

Section 3. Allows a SED professional conduct officer to examine and
obtain records of patients in any investigation or proceeding by SED
acting within the scope of its authorization. Any patient information
obtained would remain confidential unless express consent is obtained
from the patient.

Section 4. Sets for the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

SED licenses and regulates 53 licensed professions in New York State.
Currently, SED relies on licensed individuals to self report any
criminal convictions or professional misconduct findings during each
triennial re-registration period. In addition, SED has no authority to
temporarily suspend an individual's professional license, even if the
individual's conduct poses an imminent danger to the health and/or
safety of the public.

It is critically important for the health and safety of all New
Yorkers that, in the event that wrong doing or harm occurs, SED have
the proper procedures in place to respond to these incidents. This
legislation will help enhance and strengthen SED's disciplinary
processes to ensure that harm to the public is minimized while
licensed individuals receive a fair hearing process.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None
 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the one hundred eightieth day after it
shall become law.

summary: Relates to access to patient or client records in the investigation and prosecution of professional licensing and misconduct proceedings and summary suspension of professional licenses; creates a moral conduct requirement for criminal history records search for admission to a practice of a profession in this state; makes related provisions.
